problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13931905/assets/96b22799c75a4b19df4c6bddf8b63d11a7d0cab8a0cc481b8466a29eb1a2af15.png)

The diagram above shows the unit circle. Given that the $y$-coordinate of the point $P$ is $\frac{3\sqrt{5}}{7},$ use the Pythagorean identity to find $tan⁡\theta .$
worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13931905/assets/21170c11aa5ff0ab39b86f94588e5e8a0fa178d0c34b9aa1774ee9f07a4d0812.png)

Any point $(x,y)$ on the unit circle is related to the central angle $\theta $ as follows:

$$
x=cos⁡\theta ,\,y=sin⁡\theta 
$$

We're given that $y=\frac{3\sqrt{5}}{7}$ at the point $P.$ Therefore, we have

$$
sin⁡\theta =\frac{3\sqrt{5}}{7}.
$$

We can use the Pythagorean identity to find $cos⁡\theta :$

$$
\begin{aligned}{sin}^{2}⁡\theta +{cos}^{2}⁡\theta  & =1 \\ {cos}^{2}⁡\theta  & =1-{sin}^{2}⁡\theta  \\ cos⁡\theta  & =\pm \sqrt{1-{sin}^{2}⁡\theta }\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $sin⁡\theta =\frac{3\sqrt{5}}{7}$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}cos⁡\theta  & =\pm \sqrt{1-{(\frac{3\sqrt{5}}{7})}^{2}} \\  & =\pm \sqrt{1-\frac{45}{49}} \\  & =\pm \sqrt{\frac{4}{49}} \\  & =\pm \frac{2}{7}.\end{aligned}
$$

We select the positive answer since $cos⁡\theta $ is positive in the first quadrant. So, $cos⁡\theta =\frac{2}{7}.$

Finally, knowing that $tan⁡\theta =\frac{sin⁡\theta }{cos⁡\theta },$ we have

$$
tan⁡\theta =\frac{(\frac{3\sqrt{5}}{7})}{(\frac{2}{7})}=\frac{3\sqrt{5}}{2}.
$$

The diagram above shows the unit circle. Given that the y-coordinate of the point P is 357, use the Pythagorean identity to find tan⁡θ.

b
352
c

d

Correct
EXPLANATION

Any point (x,y) on the unit circle is related to the central angle θ as follows:

x=cos⁡θ,y=sin⁡θ

We're given that y=357 at the point P. Therefore, we have

sin⁡θ=357.

We can use the Pythagorean identity to find cos⁡θ:

sin2⁡θ+cos2⁡θ=1cos2⁡θ=1−sin2⁡θcos⁡θ=±1−sin2⁡θ

Substituting sin⁡θ=357 gives

cos⁡θ=±1−(357)2=±1−4549=±449=±27.

We select the positive answer since cos⁡θ is positive in the first quadrant. So, cos⁡θ=27.

Finally, knowing that tan⁡θ=sin⁡θcos⁡θ, we have tan⁡θ=(357)(27)=352.
